result.text:
The Unitree G1 and the Booster K1 are both compact, cutting-edge humanoid robots designed for research, AI development, and general robotics exploration, but they target slightly different form factors, scale, and performance metrics.

Key Comparison

Height & Form Factor

Unitree G1: Stands taller at roughly 1.32 m (4'2") and folds down for transport.
Booster K1: Significantly smaller and lighter, standing at 95 cm (under 3'3").

Weight

Unitree G1: Weighs about 35 kg (75 lbs).
Booster K1: Weighs a much lighter 19.5 kg.

Degrees of Freedom (DoF)

Unitree G1: Highly modular, ranging from 23 up to 43 DoF depending on whether you opt for advanced waist joints and multi-fingered dexterous hands.
Booster K1: Fixed at 22 DoF (12 in the legs, 8 in the arms, and 2 in the head).

Payload & Power

Unitree G1: Offers up to a 3 kg arm payload, knee joint torque up to 120 N⋅m, and roughly 2 hours of active movement runtime.
Booster K1: Geared towards lighter tasks with a smaller magnetic battery providing around a 70-minute runtime.

Computing & Sensors

Unitree G1: Equipped with Intel depth sensing, a Livox 360 Lidar, and NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX (approx. 100 TOPS) on EDU variants.
Booster K1: Scalable compute options ranging from Qualcomm QCS8550 (48 TOPS) up to a beefy NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin (200 TOPS) on Pro versions, paired with stereo depth cameras and a 9-axis IMU.

If you're deciding between them, let me know if this is for higher education/research, competitive robotics (like RoboCup), or general AI integration, and I can set up a task to track new spec updates or pricing shifts for both models.
